title: Film Your Lights in Slow Motion #science #tech
description:
Point your phone at a ceiling light and switch to slow motion. Some lights pulse, brightening and dimming 100 or 120 times a second: twice the frequency of the power in your wall (50 or 60 Hz). Your eyes blend it into a steady glow, but the camera's short exposures catch the dips. Well-made LEDs barely flicker; cheap or dimmed ones often do.

Tip: 240 frames per second shows it best; at 120 fps a 120 Hz flicker can hide.

More: Episode 50 (long, why cameras see flicker)

Sources

- ENTTEC, Why do LEDs flicker on camera? (support.enttec.com)

- The pulse in the animation is slowed far more than a real 240 fps clip shows it

Try it: film three lights in your home in slow motion. Which ones pulse?
